name: head
description: Prints the first lines (or bytes) of each input file.

flags.description: Print the first N bytes instead of lines.
Never print filename headers when multiple files are given.

examples.explanation: Prints the first 10 lines of the log.
Prints the first 20 lines — useful for previewing a CSV and checking its header row.
Shows the first 512 bytes as hex — a quick way to inspect a binary header.

about: head reads from the beginning and stops early, which makes it cheap even on huge files. With multiple files it prints a ==> filename <== header before each one.
useCases: Sample the start of large logs or datasets.
Combine with tail to print middle sections.
mistakes: Expecting head -5 to work everywhere — POSIX requires head -n 5; the -5 shorthand is a common GNU/BSD extension that usually works but is not portable.
